newsitem.title: INDIA: Manmohan Singh to brief India's Congress on budget.
newsitem.headline: Manmohan Singh to brief India's Congress on budget.

text.p: Former finance minister Manmohan Singh will brief his Congress party colleagues on Thursday on the United Front government's budget proposals for fiscal 1997/98 (April-March), the Press Trust of India said.

The Congress party, which reluctantly supports Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's 15-party coalition in parliament, has called the meeting of its Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP) to take a position on the budget presented on February 28, it said.

Singh has said that the euphoria generated by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram's bold budget proposals could be short-lived if issues like money supply and a burgeoning oil pool deficit were not handled with care.
It was not immediately clear if the CPP, which is headed by party president Sitaram Kesri, would issue a formal statement on its stand on the budget after Singh's briefing.

Several Congress deputies have publicly welcomed the 1997/98 budget which sharply cut individual and corporate taxes and nudged industry towards growth further along the path of economic reforms charted by Singh in 1991.
